g.text: active OPEN / create TCB, snd SYN
active OPEN / create TCB, snd SYN
A state IS a TCP connection state (RFC 9293 §3.3.2); the two CLOSED states are one state drawn twice — only this label says so
Connection-setup transition — opening the connection (OPEN, SYN exchange, first ACK)
Active-close path (typically the client) — calls CLOSE first: FIN-WAIT-1 → FIN-WAIT-2 / CLOSING → TIME-WAIT → CLOSED
Passive-close path (typically the server) — receives the peer's FIN first: CLOSE-WAIT → LAST-ACK → CLOSED
Rare / simultaneous transition — simultaneous open or close, or a reset/abort (RST, close from a half-open state)

svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.2 statechart title "TCP Connection State Machine (RFC 9293, Figure 5)"
# ── What this figure is ───────────────────────────────────────────── # The complete TCP connection state machine from RFC 9293 §3.3.2, # Figure 5: all 11 states and every state transition, each labelled # "event / action" exactly as the RFC writes it. `x` is the RFC's own # notation for "no action". This is the hardest showcase figure — it # answers the maintainer question "can FigDown fully express the TCP # state machine with its transitions and conditions?" — and the answer # it gives is: yes, every state is a `state` line and every labelled # transition is a `transition` line, so a reading agent recovers the # whole machine from the text. # # STATE-NESS IS FIRST-CLASS NOW, AND WAS NOT WHEN THIS FIGURE WAS # WRITTEN. Until v0.2.0 this file declared `figdown 0.1 flowchart` and # the fact "this node is a protocol state" was carried by the `states` # class label rather than by the genre. `statechart` LANDED at # 0.2 (`STATECHART-GENRE-SCOPE`) and took its own two words (`GENRE-NODE-SPELLING`) — # `state` and `transition`, whole from OMG UML 2.5.1 §14 — so the # machine-declarable fact this figure once could not state, it now # states. What follows is the ONE limit that survived that. # # HONEST LIMIT — the CLOSED identity (`IDENTITY-ASSERTION`). The canonical RFC figure # draws CLOSED TWICE — top (origin) and bottom (the terminus TIME-WAIT # and LAST-ACK return to) — and so do we, because taking every terminal # transition back to a single top state produced long lines that struck the # setup-abort labels around CLOSED and made the figure unreadable. But # FigDown CANNOT declare two elements to be the SAME entity: there is no # node-identity / alias construct (`IDENTITY-ASSERTION`). So `closed` and `closed2` # are two states that a human reads as one only because the shared # `states` class label SAYS "the two CLOSED states are one state drawn # twice." # A reading agent sees two ids; the identity is asserted # in the label, not machine-declarable. This is the single fact this # figure cannot carry that the canonical drawing implies by reusing the # name — documented, not hidden. Concretely: this figure declares 12 # `state` lines and TCP has 11 states. Merging `closed2` into `closed` # was TRIED and REJECTED — every terminal transition then ran the length of # the canvas and struck the setup/abort labels around the single CLOSED, # and the figure became unreadable. So this is evidence that the # primitive is MISSING, not that a workaround is available. # # WHERE ELSE THIS ONE GAP IS FILED (`OPEN-QUESTION-CITATION-STATUS`) — one primitive, three faces: # 1. spec/core.md §9 `IDENTITY-ASSERTION` — the MODEL-side statement, and still OPEN. # 2. the project’s working record, ISO 5807 Connector row — the # DRAWING of the same fact in genre flowchart, status unknown # (ISO §9.4.1 was never read here). Not a second requirement. # 3. this figure — the live instance. # spec/genres/experimental/statechart.md says what a reader may and may # not conclude from two identically-labelled states meanwhile. There is # no UML 2.5.1 §14 clause to borrow for this: UML has no "same state # drawn twice". # # HONEST LIMIT — RFC Note 2. The canonical Figure 5 OMITS the # FIN-WAIT-1 → TIME-WAIT transition and says so in its Note 2 (it occurs # when a FIN arrives that also ACKs our FIN). We DRAW it (transition # fw1→tw), # so this figure is strictly MORE complete than the canonical drawing # while carrying the same semantics the RFC prose states. Note 1 (rcv # RST → LISTEN applies only to a passively-opened SYN-RECEIVED) rides on # that transition's label.
# ── Semantic classes — the meaning behind every stroke ────────────── # A reading agent queries these to group transitions by role; the # colour/dash is only presentation (`MEANING-RECOVERY-SOURCE`), the meaning is the label. class states "A state IS a TCP connection state (RFC 9293 §3.3.2); the two CLOSED states are one state drawn twice — only this label says so" fill=#eef2ff class setup "Connection-setup transition — opening the connection (OPEN, SYN exchange, first ACK)" stroke=#2563eb class client "Active-close path (typically the client) — calls CLOSE first: FIN-WAIT-1 → FIN-WAIT-2 / CLOSING → TIME-WAIT → CLOSED" stroke=#dc2626 class server "Passive-close path (typically the server) — receives the peer's FIN first: CLOSE-WAIT → LAST-ACK → CLOSED" stroke=#16a34a class rare "Rare / simultaneous transition — simultaneous open or close, or a reset/abort (RST, close from a half-open state)" stroke=#9333ea style=dashed
# ── The 11 states (CLOSED drawn twice; see `IDENTITY-ASSERTION` note above) ──────── state closed "CLOSED" class=states state listen "LISTEN" class=states state synsent "SYN-SENT" class=states state synrcvd "SYN-RECEIVED" class=states state estab "ESTABLISHED" class=states state fw1 "FIN-WAIT-1" class=states state fw2 "FIN-WAIT-2" class=states state closing "CLOSING" class=states state closewait "CLOSE-WAIT" class=states state lastack "LAST-ACK" class=states state timewait "TIME-WAIT" class=states state closed2 "CLOSED" class=states
flow down
# ── Opening the connection (setup) ────────────────────────────────── transition closed -[passive OPEN / create TCB]-> listen class=setup transition closed -[active OPEN / create TCB, snd SYN]-> synsent class=setup transition listen -[SEND / snd SYN]-> synsent class=setup transition listen -[rcv SYN / snd SYN,ACK]-> synrcvd class=setup transition synsent -[rcv SYN / snd SYN,ACK]-> synrcvd class=rare transition synsent -[rcv SYN,ACK / snd ACK]-> estab class=setup transition synrcvd -[rcv ACK of SYN / x]-> estab class=setup
# ── Aborting a half-open connection (rare / reset) ────────────────── transition listen -[CLOSE / delete TCB]-> closed class=rare transition synsent -[CLOSE / delete TCB]-> closed class=rare transition synrcvd -[rcv RST (note 1) / x]-> listen class=rare
# ── Active close — the endpoint that calls CLOSE first ────────────── transition synrcvd -[CLOSE / snd FIN]-> fw1 class=client transition estab -[CLOSE / snd FIN]-> fw1 class=client transition fw1 -[rcv ACK of FIN / x]-> fw2 class=client transition fw1 -[rcv FIN / snd ACK]-> closing class=client transition fw1 -[rcv FIN,ACK / snd ACK]-> timewait class=rare transition fw2 -[rcv FIN / snd ACK]-> timewait class=client transition closing -[rcv ACK of FIN / x]-> timewait class=client transition timewait -[Timeout=2MSL / delete TCB]-> closed2 class=client
# ── Passive close — the endpoint that receives the peer's FIN ─────── transition estab -[rcv FIN / snd ACK]-> closewait class=server transition closewait -[CLOSE / snd FIN]-> lastack class=server transition lastack -[rcv ACK of FIN / x]-> closed2 class=server
layout # ── Presentation only (`GUI-WRITEBACK-STRUCTURE`) ───────────────────────────────────────── # The strip test holds: delete every line below and the machine is # unchanged — all 11 states, all 21 transitions and their event/action # labels live in the `state`/`transition`/`class` lines above (closed2 # is not an orphan: it is the target of two terminal transitions). # the layout namespace is `pin` alone, so "every line below" is a shorter # list than it used to be. # # The grid reproduces the CANONICAL Figure 5 composition, mirrored about # one central vertical axis (x≈430, the shared centre of LISTEN and # ESTABLISHED): # row0 CLOSED · row1 LISTEN · row2 SYN-RECEIVED | SYN-SENT (a mirrored # pair) · row3 ESTABLISHED · row4 FIN-WAIT-1 | CLOSE-WAIT (same mirror) # · row4½ CLOSING · row5 FIN-WAIT-2, LAST-ACK · row6 TIME-WAIT, CLOSED # (terminus, under LAST-ACK as the RFC draws it). # # COLUMN DISCIPLINE, AS IT ACTUALLY IS. This block used to # claim four dead-vertical chains and only two of them were: measuring # the centres found SYN-RECEIVED→FIN-WAIT-1 off by 32 px and # CLOSE-WAIT→LAST-ACK off by 7 px, both of which had been read as # vertical since the pins were written. A comment that names a chain the # pins below it do not honour is worse than no comment, so this is the # measured list and nothing else is claimed: # DEAD VERTICAL FIN-WAIT-1→FIN-WAIT-2 (centre x 209 both) # LAST-ACK→CLOSED (732.8 / 732.6) # DEAD HORIZONTAL SYN-SENT→SYN-RECEIVED (centre y 328 both) — the # simultaneous-open transition, across the mirrored pair # NEAR, NOT DEAD CLOSE-WAIT→LAST-ACK (7.2 px), the passive-close column # DELIBERATELY OFF-AXIS CLOSED (535.6) sits right of the LISTEN column # (429.6), and CLOSING (439.2) right of TIME-WAIT (350.4) # The last row is the 0.4 pin change and both offsets are load- # bearing, not taste. CLOSED sat dead above LISTEN, which ran the # CLOSED↔SYN-SENT diagonal pair straight through the `passive OPEN / # create TCB` label on the CLOSED→LISTEN line; moving CLOSED right (and # LISTEN 50 px down) gives each of `CLOSE / delete TCB`, `passive OPEN / # create TCB` and `active OPEN / create TCB, snd SYN` its own line to # belong to. CLOSING sat dead above TIME-WAIT, and that vertical ran # through the `rcv FIN,ACK / snd ACK` label of the FIN-WAIT-1→TIME-WAIT # diagonal (RFC Note 2's transition); lifting CLOSING up and right opens # the channel that label needs. Measured: `layout-lint` lblcol 2→0 and # F5 1→0, figure score 4→0. # DROPPING FIN-WAIT-2 DEEPER WAS TRIED AND REJECTED. It is the obvious # way to widen the same channel, and the measurement says it never is: # across 150 combinations of CLOSING and TIME-WAIT positions taken at # y=690 and y=700, FIN-WAIT-2 deeper is worse in 30 and better in NONE. # What goes wrong is the neighbour: the FIN-WAIT-2→TIME-WAIT diagonal # shortens onto its own `rcv FIN / snd ACK` label. At the pins used here # it costs exactly one lblcol strike. FIN-WAIT-2 stays on row 5 at y=670. # All meaning is in the transitions; this is layout, not knowledge. # # WHAT CHANGED, AND WHY THE TOP ROWS ARE WIDER. # Hand-routed corridors used to sit below these pins: the active # OPEN hugged the right margin with two elbows, and the two aborts back # to the top CLOSED bowed out on the outer left and outer right. The # whole construct was WITHDRAWN from the language (`EDGE-GEOMETRY-CONSTRUCTS`) — see # spec/migrations.md 0.1 and core §9 `EDGE-IDENTITY-AND-GEOMETRY` — so those three # transitions now draw straight, which puts each of them alongside its # own anti-parallel partner: CLOSED↔LISTEN and CLOSED↔SYN-SENT each # became a near-parallel pair whose two labels landed on top of one # another. The linter could not see it (0 crossings either way); a # rendered comparison could. # The fix is content-zone geometry, not a replacement for the waypoints: # rows 1 and 2 gained 20 px and 10 px, and the right-hand column moved # ~90 px further out, which pushes the two pairs' label midpoints far # enough apart to read. Both pairs still run close together, exactly as # the LISTEN↔SYN-RECEIVED pair always has in this figure — the ±7 px # anti-parallel fan-out is the language's answer to a same-pair transition, and # the class colours (blue = setup, purple = rare) say which stroke is # which. pin closed at=(500,20) pin listen at=(394,220) pin synrcvd at=(120,290) pin synsent at=(700,290) pin estab at=(376,410) pin fw1 at=(159,540) pin closewait at=(690,540) pin fw2 at=(159,670) pin closing at=(400,620) pin lastack at=(690,670) pin timewait at=(304,800) pin closed2 at=(697,800)
